applicationInfo.name: A2A Multi-Agent Orchestration Platform
applicationInfo.description:
### Summary
Agent-to-Agent orchestration platform enabling multi-agent collaboration for AWS infrastructure monitoring and web search. Built on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Runtime with Google ADK, OpenAI Agents SDK, and AWS Strands frameworks.

### Key objectives
- Enable autonomous agent-to-agent communication using A2A protocol
- Orchestrate specialized agents for monitoring and web search tasks
- Provide secure, authenticated multi-agent workflows
- Support real-time streaming responses with tool invocation visibility
- Maintain conversational memory across agent interactions

### Use-cases
- AWS CloudWatch monitoring and log analysis via specialized monitoring agent
- Web search for AWS documentation and best practices
- Incident response orchestration across multiple specialized agents
- Real-time infrastructure health monitoring with contextual memory
- Multi-framework agent integration (ADK, OpenAI Agents, Strands)

### Features
- Host agent orchestrating multiple sub-agents (Google ADK)
- Monitoring agent with CloudWatch integration (AWS Strands)
- Web search agent with memory capabilities (OpenAI Agents SDK)
- AWS Cognito authentication with JWT authorization
- Real-time streaming chat interface with React frontend
- Agent memory using BedrockAgentCore Memory service
- MCP Gateway for CloudWatch operations
- Docker-based agent deployment on ECR
- X-Ray tracing and CloudWatch logging
- OAuth2 M2M authentication between agents

architecture.description:
### High Level Architecture

#### Application type
Multi-agent AI orchestration platform with web interface

#### Layers
- Presentation: React SPA frontend
- Orchestration: Host agent (Google ADK)
- Agent: Specialized agents (Monitoring, Web Search)
- Integration: MCP Gateway for CloudWatch
- Data: Memory service, CloudWatch

#### Boundaries
- Internet to frontend (users)
- Frontend to Bedrock AgentCore Runtime (authenticated)
- Host agent to sub-agents (A2A protocol, M2M OAuth2)
- Monitoring agent to MCP Gateway (authenticated)
- MCP Gateway to CloudWatch (IAM)

#### Technology components
- Frontend: React, Vite, AWS Amplify, TypeScript
- Agents: Python (Google ADK, AWS Strands, OpenAI Agents SDK)
- Runtime: Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, Docker containers on ECR
- Auth: AWS Cognito (JWT, OAuth2 M2M)
- AI: Claude Sonnet 4.5 via Bedrock
- Observability: X-Ray, CloudWatch Logs
- IaC: CloudFormation, CodeBuild

#### Deployment architecture
- ECR repositories for agent containers (ARM64)
- CodeBuild for Docker image builds
- EventBridge for automated runtime updates
- Lambda functions for custom resources
- S3 for source code and Smithy models

#### APIs
| Endpoint | Method | Purpose |
|----------|--------|----------|
| /runtimes/{arn}/invocations | POST | Invoke agent with streaming |
| /.well-known/agent-card.json | GET | Agent capability discovery |
| /oauth2/token | POST | Cognito M2M token |
| CloudWatch Logs API | Various | Log operations via MCP |
| CloudWatch API | Various | Metrics/alarms via MCP |

#### Security relevant components
- Cognito User Pool with JWT authorizer
- OAuth2 M2M client credentials flow
- Custom header X-Amzn-Bedrock-AgentCore-Runtime-Custom-Actorid
- Secrets Manager for client credentials
- IAM roles with scoped permissions

### Low Level Architecture
- Host Agent Runtime: Google ADK-based orchestrator, HTTP protocol, public network
- Monitoring Agent Runtime: AWS Strands-based, A2A protocol, custom memory strategies
- Web Search Agent Runtime: OpenAI Agents SDK, Tavily integration, semantic memory
- MCP Gateway: Smithy model-based CloudWatch operations proxy
- Cognito: 4 clients (Web, Host, Monitoring, Gateway) with scoped OAuth2
- Memory Service: Custom extraction/consolidation for monitoring and search
- Frontend: JWT extraction, session management, SSE streaming
- Lambda Functions: ECR notification, X-Ray setup, OAuth2 provider creation
- CodeBuild: Parallel Docker build and ECR auth, ARM64 architecture

dataflow.description:
### Human actors
- End users accessing web interface for agent interactions
- AWS administrators managing infrastructure and deployments
- DevOps engineers deploying code and managing CI/CD

### External entities
- Amazon Bedrock (Claude Sonnet 4.5 model)
- Tavily web search API (via web search agent)
- AWS CloudWatch Logs and Metrics
- Amazon Cognito OAuth2 token endpoint

### Processes
- React Frontend SPA: User interface for chat interactions
- Host Agent Runtime: Orchestrates sub-agents using Google ADK
- Monitoring Agent Runtime: CloudWatch operations via AWS Strands
- Web Search Agent Runtime: Web search using OpenAI Agents SDK
- MCP Gateway: Proxy for CloudWatch API operations
- CodeBuild: Docker image build and push to ECR
- Lambda Functions: Custom resource handlers and runtime updates

### Data stores
| Store | Type | High-Value (Y/N) |
|-------|------|------------------|
| ECR Repositories | Container Registry | Y |
| CloudWatch Logs | Log Storage | Y |
| Secrets Manager | Credential Store | Y |
| SSM Parameter Store | Configuration Store | N |
| Cognito User Pool | Identity Store | Y |
| BedrockAgentCore Memory | Conversation State | Y |
| In-Memory Session Service | Session State | N |

### Trust boundaries
| Zone | Elements | Trust Level |
|------|----------|-------------|
| Public Internet | End users, Frontend | Untrusted |
| AWS Cloud - Frontend | React SPA, Amplify | Low Trust |
| AWS Cloud - Agent Runtime | Host, Monitoring, Web Search Agents | Medium Trust |
| AWS Cloud - Backend Services | Bedrock, CloudWatch, Cognito | High Trust |
| AWS Cloud - Data Layer | ECR, Secrets Manager, Memory Service | High Trust |

### Data flows
| Flow ID | Description | Source | Target | Trust Boundaries Crossed | Assets |
|---------|-------------|--------|--------|--------------------------|--------|
| DF-01 | User authentication | Frontend | Cognito | Public to AWS Cloud | JWT tokens, credentials |
| DF-02 | Agent invocation request | Frontend | Host Agent Runtime | Frontend to Agent Runtime | User prompts, session IDs, JWT |
| DF-03 | Streaming response | Host Agent Runtime | Frontend | Agent Runtime to Frontend | Agent responses, tool outputs |
| DF-04 | Sub-agent invocation | Host Agent | Monitoring/Web Search Agent | Agent Runtime (internal) | Prompts, A2A protocol messages |
| DF-05 | M2M token request | Agent Runtime | Cognito | Agent Runtime to Backend | Client credentials, OAuth2 tokens |
| DF-06 | CloudWatch operations | Monitoring Agent | MCP Gateway | Agent Runtime (internal) | Log queries, metric requests |
| DF-07 | CloudWatch API calls | MCP Gateway | CloudWatch | Agent Runtime to Backend | AWS API requests, log data |
| DF-08 | LLM inference | Agent Runtimes | Bedrock | Agent Runtime to Backend | Prompts, model responses |
| DF-09 | Memory operations | Agent Runtimes | Memory Service | Agent Runtime to Data Layer | Conversation context, technical issues |
| DF-10 | Docker image push | CodeBuild | ECR | Backend (internal) | Container images |
| DF-11 | Runtime update trigger | EventBridge | Lambda | Backend (internal) | ECR push events |
| DF-12 | Runtime configuration update | Lambda | Agent Runtime | Backend (internal) | Container URIs, config |
| DF-13 | Web search query | Web Search Agent | Tavily API | AWS Cloud to Public Internet | Search queries, results |
| DF-14 | X-Ray traces | Agent Runtimes | X-Ray | Agent Runtime to Backend | Distributed traces |
| DF-15 | Application logs | Agent Runtimes | CloudWatch Logs | Agent Runtime to Backend | Log events, errors |

mitigations.content: Implement prompt injection detection using Amazon Bedrock Guardrails with content filtering and denied topics to block malicious prompts attempting to extract memory data or manipulate agent behavior

metadata.value:
**Implementation**: Configure Bedrock Guardrails with custom denied topics for memory extraction patterns, system prompt override attempts, and data exfiltration keywords. Apply guardrails to all agent invocations before processing.

**Rationale**: Addresses prompt injection at the entry point before prompts reach the LLM. Bedrock Guardrails provides native integration with Claude models and can detect adversarial patterns.

**Considerations**: Requires tuning to avoid false positives. Monitor guardrail rejection rates and adjust policies based on legitimate use cases.

mitigations.content: Enforce actor-based memory isolation by validating JWT sub claim against memory service queries and implementing server-side access controls to prevent cross-actor memory access

metadata.value:
**Implementation**: Add middleware to agent runtime that extracts and validates JWT sub claim, then enforces that all memory service queries include actor ID filter. Implement memory service access controls that reject queries without proper actor scoping.

**Rationale**: Prevents attackers with valid tokens from accessing other users' conversation history or technical issues stored in memory.

**Considerations**: Requires modification to memory service client code and potential updates to BedrockAgentCore Memory API calls to enforce scoping.

mitigations.content: Implement rate limiting using AWS WAF for frontend endpoints and API Gateway throttling for agent runtime invocations with per-user quotas based on JWT sub claim

metadata.value:
**Implementation**: Deploy AWS WAF in front of frontend with rate-based rules (e.g., 100 requests per 5 minutes per IP). Configure agent runtime with throttling limits (e.g., 10 concurrent invocations per user). Use JWT sub claim for user-level rate limiting.

**Rationale**: Prevents DoS attacks and resource exhaustion from high-volume concurrent requests. Protects both Bedrock API quotas and agent runtime resources.

**Considerations**: Set appropriate limits based on expected usage patterns. Monitor for legitimate users hitting limits and adjust accordingly.

mitigations.content: Enable Cognito Advanced Security Features including adaptive authentication, compromised credentials detection, and require MFA for all user accounts accessing agent invocation capabilities

metadata.value:
**Implementation**: Enable Cognito Advanced Security in User Pool configuration. Configure MFA using TOTP or SMS. Enable compromised credentials check against known breach databases. Implement adaptive authentication to require step-up authentication for sensitive operations.

**Rationale**: Significantly reduces risk of credential stuffing, brute force, and account takeover attacks. Adaptive authentication adds context-aware security.

**Considerations**: User experience impact from MFA enrollment. Consider phased rollout starting with high-privilege users.

mitigations.content: Implement automatic secret rotation for M2M client credentials in Secrets Manager with 90-day rotation period and update OAuth2 credential providers to use rotated secrets

metadata.value:
**Implementation**: Configure Secrets Manager automatic rotation using Lambda rotation function. Update Cognito app client secrets on rotation. Modify OAuth2 credential providers to fetch secrets from Secrets Manager on each token request rather than caching.

**Rationale**: Limits exposure window if M2M credentials are compromised. Reduces risk of long-term credential theft from Secrets Manager.

**Considerations**: Requires coordination between secret rotation and agent runtime credential refresh. Test rotation process thoroughly to avoid service disruption.

mitigations.content: Implement least-privilege IAM policies for Secrets Manager access with resource-level permissions restricting each agent to only its own client credentials

metadata.value:
**Implementation**: Create separate IAM policies for each agent runtime that grant GetSecretValue only for their specific secret ARN. Remove wildcard permissions. Implement IAM condition keys to restrict access by resource tags.

**Rationale**: Prevents lateral movement where compromised agent credentials allow access to other agents' secrets. Limits blast radius of credential compromise.

**Considerations**: Review and update CloudFormation templates to implement granular IAM policies. Test each agent runtime can only access its designated secrets.

mitigations.content: Enable ECR image scanning with automatic scanning on push and implement admission control to block deployment of images with HIGH or CRITICAL vulnerabilities

metadata.value:
**Implementation**: Enable ECR enhanced scanning (Inspector integration) for all repositories. Modify ECRImageNotificationFunction Lambda to check scan results before updating runtime. Reject runtime updates if scan finds HIGH/CRITICAL vulnerabilities.

**Rationale**: Prevents deployment of vulnerable container images that could be exploited. Provides continuous vulnerability assessment of agent runtime containers.

**Considerations**: May require vulnerability remediation workflow. Consider grace period for existing vulnerabilities with compensating controls.

mitigations.content: Implement Docker image signing using AWS Signer and verify image signatures in Lambda function before updating agent runtime configuration

metadata.value:
**Implementation**: Configure AWS Signer signing profile for container images. Update CodeBuild to sign images after build using docker trust sign. Modify ECRImageNotificationFunction to verify image signature using AWS Signer API before updating runtime.

**Rationale**: Ensures only images built by authorized CodeBuild project are deployed. Prevents deployment of malicious images pushed directly to ECR.

**Considerations**: Requires integration with AWS Signer and modification to build pipeline. Test signature verification thoroughly to avoid blocking legitimate deployments.

mitigations.content: Implement EventBridge rule conditions to validate ECR push events originate from authorized CodeBuild project ARN before triggering Lambda runtime updates

metadata.value:
**Implementation**: Add event pattern filtering to EventBridge rule that checks detail.requestParameters.sourceArn matches authorized CodeBuild project ARN. Implement additional validation in Lambda to verify event source and reject unauthorized updates.

**Rationale**: Prevents attackers from triggering runtime updates with crafted EventBridge events. Ensures only legitimate build pipeline can update agent containers.

**Considerations**: Requires understanding of ECR push event structure. Test with actual CodeBuild pushes to ensure legitimate events are not blocked.

mitigations.content: Implement resource-based policy on Lambda functions to restrict invocation to EventBridge rules and require event signature validation

metadata.value:
**Implementation**: Add Lambda resource-based policy that allows invocation only from specific EventBridge rule ARNs. Remove any wildcard permissions. Implement event signature validation in Lambda code to verify events are authentic.

**Rationale**: Prevents direct Lambda invocation by unauthorized actors. Ensures Lambda functions can only be triggered through legitimate EventBridge rules.

**Considerations**: Review all Lambda functions that handle sensitive operations (ECR notifications, X-Ray setup, OAuth2 configuration). Update CloudFormation to implement restrictive policies.

mitigations.content: Implement CloudWatch Logs resource-based policies to restrict MCP Gateway access to specific log groups using IAM conditions and resource tags

metadata.value:
**Implementation**: Tag CloudWatch log groups by sensitivity level. Update MCP Gateway IAM role to include condition keys that restrict access based on resource tags. Implement deny policies for production log groups unless explicitly authorized.

**Rationale**: Limits scope of CloudWatch data accessible through monitoring agent. Prevents exfiltration of sensitive production logs even if monitoring agent credentials are compromised.

**Considerations**: Requires log group tagging strategy. May need separate monitoring agents for different environments with scoped permissions.

mitigations.content: Enable CloudWatch Logs Insights query logging and implement anomaly detection for unusual query patterns indicating data exfiltration attempts

metadata.value:
**Implementation**: Enable CloudWatch Logs query logging for all log groups accessed by MCP Gateway. Create CloudWatch Insights queries to detect anomalies like high-volume log retrieval, unusual time patterns, or queries for sensitive log groups. Set up CloudWatch Alarms for anomaly thresholds.

**Rationale**: Provides visibility into CloudWatch data access patterns. Enables detection of credential compromise or insider threats attempting data exfiltration.

**Considerations**: Requires baseline of normal query patterns. Tune detection thresholds to minimize false positives while catching genuine threats.

mitigations.content: Implement Content Security Policy (CSP) headers in frontend with strict-dynamic and nonce-based script execution to prevent XSS attacks and token theft

metadata.value:
**Implementation**: Configure web server to send CSP headers with script-src 'strict-dynamic' and nonce-based script loading. Disable unsafe-inline and unsafe-eval. Implement nonce generation in Vite build process. Add additional headers: X-Frame-Options, X-Content-Type-Options, Referrer-Policy.

**Rationale**: Prevents injection of malicious JavaScript that could steal JWT tokens from browser storage. Strict CSP significantly reduces XSS attack surface.

**Considerations**: Requires refactoring inline scripts to use nonces. Test thoroughly with all frontend features. May break third-party integrations that use inline scripts.

mitigations.content: Implement Subresource Integrity (SRI) for all external JavaScript dependencies and enable npm audit in CI/CD pipeline to block builds with known vulnerabilities

metadata.value:
**Implementation**: Configure Vite to generate SRI hashes for all script and style tags. Add npm audit check to CodeBuild buildspec that fails build if HIGH/CRITICAL vulnerabilities detected. Implement dependency scanning using npm audit or Snyk.

**Rationale**: Prevents compromised CDN or npm packages from injecting malicious code. Ensures frontend dependencies are verified before execution.

**Considerations**: Requires process for updating dependencies when vulnerabilities found. SRI may complicate dynamic script loading if used.

mitigations.content: Enable encryption at rest for BedrockAgentCore Memory service using AWS KMS customer-managed keys with key rotation and access logging

metadata.value:
**Implementation**: Configure BedrockAgentCore Memory service to use KMS CMK for encryption at rest. Enable automatic key rotation. Configure KMS key policy to restrict access to agent runtimes only. Enable CloudTrail logging for all KMS key usage.

**Rationale**: Protects conversation context and technical issue data at rest. Provides audit trail of memory data access. Key rotation limits exposure from key compromise.

**Considerations**: Verify BedrockAgentCore Memory supports CMK encryption. May have performance impact from KMS API calls. Monitor KMS costs and request limits.

mitigations.content: Implement memory data access logging with CloudTrail and create CloudWatch alarms for unusual memory access patterns or cross-actor access attempts

metadata.value:
**Implementation**: Enable CloudTrail data events for BedrockAgentCore Memory service API calls. Create CloudWatch Logs Insights queries to detect anomalies like high-volume memory reads, access outside normal hours, or attempts to query memories for different actors. Set up alarms for threshold breaches.

**Rationale**: Provides visibility into memory data access. Enables detection of compromised credentials or attempts to exfiltrate conversation history.

**Considerations**: CloudTrail data events can be expensive at scale. Consider sampling or filtering to critical operations only.

mitigations.content: Implement network segmentation using VPC with private subnets for agent runtimes and VPC endpoints for AWS service access to prevent internet exposure

metadata.value:
**Implementation**: Deploy agent runtimes in VPC private subnets with no internet gateway. Create VPC endpoints for Bedrock, Secrets Manager, CloudWatch, and other AWS services. Implement security groups restricting agent-to-agent communication to required ports only. Use Network ACLs for additional layer of defense.

**Rationale**: Eliminates internet-based attack vectors against agent runtimes. Prevents data exfiltration to external endpoints. Reduces risk of man-in-the-middle attacks on A2A protocol.

**Considerations**: Requires VPC configuration in CloudFormation. May need NAT Gateway for outbound internet access (e.g., Tavily API). Test all agent communication paths work through VPC endpoints.

mitigations.content: Enable VPC Flow Logs and implement network traffic analysis to detect anomalous communication patterns between agents or data exfiltration attempts

metadata.value:
**Implementation**: Enable VPC Flow Logs for all subnets containing agent runtimes. Send logs to CloudWatch Logs. Create CloudWatch Insights queries to detect anomalies like unexpected destination IPs, high-volume data transfers, or communication outside normal patterns. Use Amazon GuardDuty VPC Flow Log analysis.

**Rationale**: Provides visibility into network-level threats. Enables detection of compromised agents attempting lateral movement or data exfiltration.

**Considerations**: VPC Flow Logs can generate significant data volume. Consider filtering to rejected traffic or specific security groups. Use sampling if cost is concern.

mitigations.content: Implement S3 bucket policies with encryption enforcement and versioning for Smithy model storage, with CloudTrail logging of all object modifications

metadata.value:
**Implementation**: Configure S3 bucket policy requiring encryption for all PutObject operations. Enable versioning to maintain history of Smithy model changes. Enable S3 Object Lock to prevent deletion. Configure CloudTrail to log all S3 data events. Implement IAM policies restricting write access to authorized deployment roles only.

**Rationale**: Prevents unauthorized modification of Smithy model that defines MCP Gateway operations. Provides audit trail and ability to rollback malicious changes.

**Considerations**: Versioning increases storage costs. Implement lifecycle policy to archive old versions. Test MCP Gateway handles model updates correctly.

mitigations.content: Implement Smithy model validation in MCP Gateway startup that verifies model signature and checksums before loading operations

metadata.value:
**Implementation**: Generate and store cryptographic hash of approved Smithy model in SSM Parameter Store. Modify MCP Gateway startup code to download model, compute hash, and compare against stored value. Reject startup if hash mismatch. Implement model signing using AWS Signer.

**Rationale**: Detects tampering with Smithy model before malicious operations can be exposed. Ensures MCP Gateway only loads authorized CloudWatch operation definitions.

**Considerations**: Requires process for updating hash when model legitimately changes. Consider using AWS Signer for more robust signature verification.

mitigations.content: Implement IAM policies with explicit deny for sensitive Bedrock operations and enforce resource-based policies requiring specific agent runtime ARNs

metadata.value:
**Implementation**: Create IAM policies with explicit deny for Bedrock model management operations (CreateModel, DeleteModel, etc.). Implement condition keys requiring requests come from specific agent runtime ARNs. Use AWS Organizations SCPs to enforce policies across accounts.

**Rationale**: Prevents compromised credentials from being used for unauthorized Bedrock operations. Limits blast radius of credential compromise to agent invocation only.

**Considerations**: Review all Bedrock API operations and determine which should be explicitly denied. Test agent runtimes can still perform legitimate inference operations.

mitigations.content: Enable AWS CloudTrail for Bedrock API calls and implement CloudWatch alarms for high-volume inference requests or unusual usage patterns

metadata.value:
**Implementation**: Enable CloudTrail logging for all Bedrock API calls. Create CloudWatch metrics from logs tracking invocation count, token usage, and error rates per agent. Set up alarms for anomalies like sudden spike in invocations, high error rates, or usage outside normal hours.

**Rationale**: Provides visibility into Bedrock usage and enables detection of compromised credentials or DoS attacks. Helps identify quota exhaustion risks.

**Considerations**: CloudTrail logs can be expensive for high-volume APIs. Consider filtering to specific operations or using CloudWatch metrics instead of full logging.

mitigations.content: Implement CodeBuild source integrity validation using CodeCommit branch protection and require signed commits for all code changes

metadata.value:
**Implementation**: If using CodeCommit, enable branch protection requiring pull request reviews and signed commits. Configure CodeBuild to verify commit signatures before build. Implement approval workflow requiring security review for changes to buildspec.yml or Dockerfiles.

**Rationale**: Prevents unauthorized modification of build process. Ensures only approved code changes are built and deployed to agent runtimes.

**Considerations**: Requires Git signing setup for all developers. May slow down development workflow. Consider automated security scanning in PR process.

mitigations.content: Implement input validation and sanitization for web search queries to prevent injection attacks and limit query scope to approved domains

metadata.value:
**Implementation**: Add query validation in web search agent that checks for SQL injection patterns, command injection attempts, and malicious URLs. Implement allowlist of approved search domains (e.g., AWS documentation sites only). Sanitize query strings before passing to Tavily API.

**Rationale**: Prevents attackers from using web search agent to probe internal systems or exfiltrate data through search queries. Limits search scope to legitimate use cases.

**Considerations**: May limit functionality if search needs to cover broad internet. Consider implementing query review workflow for sensitive searches.

mitigations.content: Implement session timeout and idle timeout policies in frontend with automatic token refresh and secure token storage using httpOnly cookies instead of localStorage

metadata.value:
**Implementation**: Configure Cognito token expiration to 1 hour. Implement frontend idle timeout (e.g., 15 minutes) that clears session. Move JWT storage from localStorage to httpOnly, Secure, SameSite cookies. Implement automatic token refresh using refresh token before expiration.

**Rationale**: Limits window of opportunity for stolen tokens. httpOnly cookies prevent JavaScript access, mitigating XSS token theft. Idle timeout reduces risk from unattended sessions.

**Considerations**: Requires backend changes to handle cookie-based authentication. May impact user experience with frequent re-authentication. Test token refresh flow thoroughly.

mitigations.content: Enable AWS GuardDuty for threat detection across EC2, S3, and IAM with automated response using EventBridge and Lambda for high-severity findings

metadata.value:
**Implementation**: Enable GuardDuty in AWS account. Configure EventBridge rules to trigger Lambda functions for high-severity findings (e.g., compromised credentials, unusual API calls). Implement automated response actions like disabling compromised IAM users, revoking tokens, or isolating compromised resources.

**Rationale**: Provides continuous threat detection using machine learning and threat intelligence. Enables rapid response to security incidents before significant damage occurs.

**Considerations**: GuardDuty has monthly costs based on data volume. Test automated response actions carefully to avoid false positive disruptions. Implement notification workflow for security team.

mitigations.content: Implement centralized security logging with CloudWatch Logs aggregation and retention policies, with automated alerting for security events using CloudWatch Insights

metadata.value:
**Implementation**: Aggregate all security-relevant logs (CloudTrail, VPC Flow Logs, application logs, X-Ray traces) into dedicated CloudWatch Log Groups. Implement 90-day retention for compliance. Create CloudWatch Insights queries for security events (failed auth, privilege escalation, unusual API calls). Set up SNS notifications for critical events.

**Rationale**: Provides centralized visibility for security monitoring and incident response. Enables correlation of events across different services. Supports compliance requirements for log retention.

**Considerations**: Log aggregation and retention costs can be significant. Consider using S3 for long-term archive with lifecycle policies. Implement log filtering to reduce noise.

mitigations.content: Implement X-Ray trace data sanitization to remove sensitive information (credentials, PII, internal IPs) before writing to CloudWatch Logs

metadata.value:
**Implementation**: Configure X-Ray SDK to use custom sampling rules that exclude sensitive annotations. Implement trace data sanitization in agent runtime code that redacts credentials, tokens, and PII before sending to X-Ray. Use X-Ray filter expressions to exclude sensitive segments.

**Rationale**: Prevents exposure of sensitive information through X-Ray traces. Reduces risk from unauthorized access to CloudWatch Logs containing trace data.

**Considerations**: May reduce debugging capabilities if too much data is sanitized. Balance security with operational needs. Test sanitization doesn't break trace analysis.

mitigations.content: Implement Lambda function versioning and aliases with gradual deployment using CodeDeploy to detect and rollback malicious code changes

metadata.value:
**Implementation**: Enable Lambda versioning for all functions. Create production alias pointing to stable version. Configure CodeDeploy for Lambda with Linear10PercentEvery1Minute deployment. Implement CloudWatch alarms monitoring error rates and invocation counts as deployment health checks. Automatic rollback on alarm.

**Rationale**: Limits blast radius of malicious Lambda code changes. Enables rapid detection and rollback if modified function exhibits anomalous behavior.

**Considerations**: Requires CloudWatch alarms tuned to detect malicious behavior vs. normal errors. May slow down deployment process. Test rollback procedures thoroughly.

mitigations.content: Implement Cognito user pool account takeover protection with risk-based authentication and automated account lockout for suspicious activity

metadata.value:
**Implementation**: Enable Cognito Advanced Security risk-based authentication. Configure account takeover protection to detect suspicious sign-ins (new device, new location, unusual time). Implement automated actions like requiring MFA, blocking sign-in, or sending notification. Configure account lockout after 5 failed attempts.

**Rationale**: Provides adaptive security that responds to authentication threats in real-time. Reduces risk of credential stuffing and account takeover.

**Considerations**: May impact legitimate users traveling or using new devices. Implement user-friendly account recovery process. Monitor false positive rates and adjust risk thresholds.
